reuse.why: It reuses getApproxNumberThreshold and getRangeAmount and replaces five server dispatches, but writes a new getExpectedAmount next to the existing exported getScheduledAmount, which already decides the missing/number/range cases, instead of extending it.

duplication.why: getExpectedAmount repeats getScheduledAmount's null -> 0, number -> as-is, range -> getRangeAmount dispatch, so the tree now has two parallel amount resolvers.

placement.why: The rule lives in shared/schedules.ts next to getRangeAmount, and the server call sites only pass their value and op.

scope.why: Only the amount resolution sites, a unit test and a release note change.

maintainability.why: Server paths are unified, but consumers of getScheduledAmount (api-models expectedAmount, client Balance/SchedulesTable/mobile) still resolve without the approx rule. A maintainer has to know which of the two near-identical helpers to call.

bypasses_abstraction.where: packages/loot-core/src/shared/schedules.ts: new getExpectedAmount sits next to getScheduledAmount instead of folding the approx rule into it; getScheduledAmount callers (server/api-models.ts expectedAmount, desktop-client Balance.tsx, SchedulesTable.tsx, mobile schedules) are untouched.

disguised_duplication.where: getExpectedAmount in shared/schedules.ts is getScheduledAmount's missing/number/range dispatch reshaped (inverse dropped, op added) under a new name.

one_place.where: The approx worst case lands in getExpectedAmount, which the server paths use (schedule-template, forecast-schedules, schedules/app updateActions and postTransactionForSchedule, computeSchedulePreviewTransactions). getScheduledAmount, used by api-models expectedAmount and the client balance and list views, still returns the exact approx value.
